 The strong growth in refined supply is mainly attributed to rising production of chemical products in China and Finland  The above has resulted in a change in the patterns of raw materials; cobalt concentrates and intermediates are used as feed for chemical production  Intermediate products are seeing robust capacity expansion as they are the preferred raw material due to higher operational and logistical efficiency  Anecdotal evidence suggests that in 2012 consumers of concentrates and intermediates have partly used cobalt metal instead Data: CRU

a strong cash position and without secured raw materials ceased operations; a combination of high production costs and low market prices impacted several small companies  Large-scale operations implemented different strategies to expand and benefit from growing demand mainly from the booming rechargeable battery sector  A major development is the growing volume of intermediates as the preferred raw material type  Industry restructuring led to consolidation, with a smaller number of operations and bigger capacity each Data: CRU © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential # Chapter 3 – Market balance & prices ## Cobalt prices continue to descend ##### US$/lb **20 15 10 RN 99.8% Co RN 99.3% Co LME 99.3% Co 5 0 05/11 08/11 11/11 02/12 05/12 08/12 11/12** Data: Ryan’s Notes, LME
 Oversupply has been weighing on prices since mid-2011, generating a negative trend  Seasonal post-summer restocking activity supported cobalt prices in August 2012; however, the revival did not last long due to a cautious sentiment in the spot market  In October-November 2012, the market overreacted to production and marketing developments at the Ambatovy operation  December 2012 saw further price declines, triggered by selling activity with a view to reducing year-end inventories © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential ## Surpluses are expected to weigh on prices in the medium term **Supply/Demand balance 99.3% nominal price**US$/lb **20 19 18** tonnes **6,000 4,000 2,000** **17 16** **0 -2,000 -4,000 -6,000 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017** **15 14 13 12** **11**  CRU believes that the prevailing negative cobalt price trend will continue until 2014  From 2014 onward, the market is expected to tighten as demand growth will outperform supply  We forecast higher market surpluses in 2014-2017 compared to the outlook we published in August; this is attributed to an upward revision in the Chinese refined production projections  As a result, our cobalt price forecast has been revised down Data: CRU © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential ## Price outlook - increased downside risks in the near/medium-term US$/lb
